2af83112f95570a7:2649.summary: Researchers investigated whether frozen, zero-shot large language models can provide retraining-free control in hierarchical cyber defense across networks of varying scales. Using the Cyberwheel environment mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, they compared various RL and LLM configurations. While replacing only the planner yielded limited gains, extending LLM control to execution produced notable improvements for capable models. Specifically, a frozen 70B model held successful lateral movement to about 1% of steps and attacker impact near zero across small, medium, and large networks without retraining.
2af83112f95570a7:2649.one_liner: Frozen 70B LLMs can act as effective tactical execution agents in hierarchical cyber defense, maintaining strong security performance across varying network scales without retraining.
2af83112f95570a7:2649.bottom_line: Capable frozen LLMs can replace retrained RL baselines for tactical execution in hierarchical cyber defense, maintaining near-zero attacker impact across different network scales.

claims.text: For instance, a frozen general purpose 70B model holds successful lateral movement to approximately 1% of steps and attacker impact near zero across all three network scales using the same model weights, while the RL baseline is retrained for each scale.
claims.support_span: For instance, a frozen general purpose 70B model holds successful lateral movement to approximately 1% of steps and attacker impact near zero across all three network scales using the same model weights, while the RL baseline is retrained for each scale.

06613c4c858abb9e:2646.summary: Safety routers that send requests to different models are typically evaluated against the best single model chosen on the evaluation data, a practice that breaks under distribution shift. The authors show that selection cost under distribution shift is substantial on HELM Safety and rises sharply on AgentDojo when suites are held out. Additionally, an attacker who knows which model they face can lower a model's recognized late injection score significantly. Scored honestly under shift, routing buys little on these benchmarks.
06613c4c858abb9e:2646.one_liner: LLM safety routing evaluations suffer from severe bias under distribution shift, and routing benefits shrink dramatically when scored honestly.
06613c4c858abb9e:2646.bottom_line: Standard LLM safety routing benchmarks provide misleadingly high performance estimates because their comparator selection breaks under distribution shift.

claims.text: On HELM Safety the selection cost is 0.003-0.030 of harm under random splits and 0.045-0.113 under held-out categories, comparable to the whole deficit attributed to routing, with its direction holding under either published judge alone.
claims.support_span: On HELM Safety the selection cost is 0.003-0.030 of harm under random splits and 0.045-0.113 under held-out categories, comparable to the whole deficit attributed to routing, with its direction holding under either published judge alone.

key_facts: HELM Safety selection cost: 0.003-0.030 under random splits
HELM Safety selection cost under held-out categories: 0.045-0.113
GPT-5.4 recognition drop under attack: 19.6 points

13713bf66ce09fa8:1987.summary: Researchers proposed MemFit, a long-term memory system for conversational agents that aims to reduce the cost and latency of memory operations. Unlike systems that rely on expensive LLM calls for construction or compress data by discarding surface details, MemFit stores each turn verbatim in an append-only store with LLM-free insertion. It uses an LLM-free multi-path retrieval strategy combining lexical and semantic signals with cross-encoder reranking. Empirical results on LoCoMo, MemGallery, and LongMemEval-S show that MemFit achieves state-of-the-art performance while reducing memory construction time and cost.
13713bf66ce09fa8:1987.one_liner: MemFit provides a scalable, LLM-free insertion and retrieval long-term memory system for conversational agents that reduces construction costs while achieving state-of-the-art performance.
13713bf66ce09fa8:1987.bottom_line: MemFit eliminates costly LLM calls during memory construction for conversational agents by using verbatim append-only stores and LLM-free multi-path retrieval.

claims.text: Unlike existing systems that rely on expensive LLM calls for memory construction or discard surface-level details through compression, MemFit stores each turn verbatim in an append-only store with near-instantaneous, LLM-free insertion, indexing turns with segment summaries rather than replacing them.
claims.support_span: Unlike existing systems that rely on expensive LLM calls for memory construction or discard surface-level details through compression, MemFit stores each turn verbatim in an append-only store with near-instantaneous, LLM-free insertion, indexing turns with segment summaries rather than replacing them.

key_facts: Evaluated benchmarks: LoCoMo, MemGallery, and LongMemEval-S

5f03340a3c340315:2738.summary: Researchers introduced RISED, a framework using rubrics for agentic multi-environment selection and self-distillation to train generalist LLM agents across diverse interactive environments. Instead of relying solely on scalar rewards, RISED uses an LLM judge to tag rollouts with a predefined rubric vocabulary to guide online data selection and policy supervision. Positive rubrics provide context for an on-policy self-distillation teacher, while negative rubrics steer generation away from recurring failure modes. Across backbones, RISED achieved the highest mean pass rate across evaluated environments.
5f03340a3c340315:2738.one_liner: RISED improves multi-environment LLM agent training by using rubric-based textual feedback for online data selection and self-distillation.
5f03340a3c340315:2738.bottom_line: Using rubric-based textual feedback instead of scalar rewards alone allows LLM agents to generalize better across diverse interactive environments.

claims.text: Across model backbones, RISED achieves the highest mean pass rate across environments and ranks first or second in every individual environment.
claims.support_span: Across model backbones, RISED achieves the highest mean pass rate across environments and ranks first or second in every individual environment.

ef5ece8fb88b20d8:2597.summary: Researchers introduced ActiveSaddler, an automated curriculum learning method for optimizing LLM agent harnesses by treating the training curriculum as a non-stationary bandit. As prompts, tool interfaces, and control logic evolve, ActiveSaddler abstracts recurring failures into reusable failure-pattern arms and dynamically balances revisiting weaknesses with exploring unseen scenarios. Experiments on GAIA2 and Terminal-Bench 2.0 showed that ActiveSaddler improved test Pass@1 by 4.4 and 7.5 percentage points, respectively, compared to a fixed scenario order.
ef5ece8fb88b20d8:2597.one_liner: ActiveSaddler co-evolves training curricula with LLM agent harnesses, boosting performance by dynamically targeting emerging failure patterns.
ef5ece8fb88b20d8:2597.bottom_line: Automated curriculum learning that dynamically adapts training scenarios alongside agent harness updates significantly improves agent optimization outcomes.

claims.text: Experiments on GAIA2 and Terminal-Bench 2.0 show that ActiveSaddler consistently discovers stronger harnesses, improving test Pass@1 by 4.4 and 7.5 percentage points over the same harness optimizer using a scenario order fixed before optimization, respectively.
claims.support_span: Experiments on GAIA2 and Terminal-Bench 2.0 show that ActiveSaddler consistently discovers stronger harnesses, improving test Pass@1 by 4.4 and 7.5 percentage points over the same harness optimizer using a scenario order fixed before optimization, respectively.

db8dbe399ef31566:2227.summary: Researchers introduced ReLiveGym, a diagnostic evaluation environment for long-lived LLM agents that operate unattended over weeks of replayed real-world news, market, and social-media streams. The evaluation highlights that action timing mechanisms and harness designs are critical for long-lived tasks where agents must act sparsely. Additionally, the study evaluated how continuous learning from hindsight feedback addresses failure modes in these environments.
db8dbe399ef31566:2227.one_liner: ReLiveGym evaluates long-lived LLM agents over simulated weeks of replayed real-world data, highlighting the importance of action timing and harness design.
db8dbe399ef31566:2227.bottom_line: Long-lived LLM agents requiring persistent monitoring must be evaluated on temporal dynamics, where action timing and feedback integration are key architectural axes.

claims.text: We introduce ReLiveGym, a diagnostic evaluation environment of long-lived tasks in which agents act sparsely over simulated weeks of chronologically replayed real-world news, market, and social-media streams.
claims.support_span: We introduce ReLiveGym, a diagnostic evaluation environment of long-lived tasks in which agents act sparsely over simulated weeks of chronologically replayed real-world news, market, and social-media streams.

1d9ebfbb76c99688:2205.summary: Researchers analyzed the shape of memory use in long-horizon language agents and discovered that under repeated retrieval, agent memory concentrates on a small core while leaving rare states in a heavy-tailed distribution. Motivated by this finding, they proposed the Core-Tail World Model (CTWM), a rank-based memory controller that allocates prompt budgets using a single exponent while retaining a summarized tail. CTWM reduces prompt token usage across benchmark environments while maintaining state coverage and task accuracy.
1d9ebfbb76c99688:2205.one_liner: CTWM leverages heavy-tailed memory traces to optimize prompt token budgets and reduce prediction error in long-horizon language agents.
1d9ebfbb76c99688:2205.bottom_line: Agent memory naturally exhibits heavy-tailed traces under finite context, which can be exploited using rank-based controllers to achieve token efficiency without accuracy loss.

claims.text: On Synthetic Graph World, CTWM preserves full state and transition coverage, reduces prompt tokens by 5.9%, and lowers bottom-half tail prediction error by 13.6% relative to a graph-memory baseline.
claims.support_span: On Synthetic Graph World, CTWM preserves full state and transition coverage, reduces prompt tokens by 5.9%, and lowers bottom-half tail prediction error by 13.6% relative to a graph-memory baseline.

a97398f76ee518bf:5389.summary: Chatham Financial integrated OpenAI's Codex and GPT-5.6 into its capital markets operations to build internal tools and reengineer client workflows. Through its Process Zero consulting service, Chatham reengineered trade validation—a process previously taking 30 minutes—using a Codex-built application that gathers evidence, compares terms, and flags discrepancies, reducing review time to under four minutes. Additionally, employees use internal platforms powered by GPT-5.6 to build applications supporting fixed-income rate sheets, hedging dashboards, and trade confirmations.
a97398f76ee518bf:5389.one_liner: Chatham Financial leverages OpenAI's Codex and GPT-5.6 to automate capital markets workflows, reducing trade validation time from 30 minutes to under four minutes.
a97398f76ee518bf:5389.bottom_line: Financial advisory firms can dramatically accelerate trade validation and operational workflows by deploying custom AI applications built with LLMs.

a3a0eec377ea25db:2250.summary: Researchers presented Kepler, an open-source harness for evaluating agents on ARC-AGI-3 that represents hypotheses as executable world models and validates them through retrospective transition checks and conditional prediction checks. Using a frozen Claude Opus 5 configuration, Kepler achieved a verified 100.00 RHAE on all 25 public games without per-game model selection. The authors also highlighted evaluation failures such as source-code leakage and autonomous repair masking a broken planner, noting that public-set scores alone have limited discriminative value.
a3a0eec377ea25db:2250.one_liner: Kepler achieves perfect scores on ARC-AGI-3 public games using auditable world models, while highlighting critical evaluation flaws in benchmark scoring.
a3a0eec377ea25db:2250.bottom_line: Auditable world models can solve interactive agent benchmarks like ARC-AGI-3, but public-set scores alone offer limited discriminative value due to hidden evaluation vulnerabilities.

claims.text: Under one frozen Claude Opus 5 configuration, Kepler obtained a server-verified 100.00 RHAE on all 25 public games, with no per-game model selection or score-conditioned reruns.
claims.support_span: Under one frozen Claude Opus 5 configuration, Kepler obtained a server-verified 100.00 RHAE on all 25 public games, with no per-game model selection or score-conditioned reruns.

02499ab677055d09:124.bottom_line: Amazon has added to the open-source model landscape with Strands Decider 2B for rapid decision-making.

0863741e9d4fb3c2:117.one_liner: Google unveils Gemini 4 Argon in a limited release, taking benchmark leads.

7313d5e64734621e:2746.summary: Self-modifying AI agents that replace, fork, or roll back identity-bearing software risk breaking permission boundaries across generations. Researchers defined authorization succession to conserve authority across a single-parent generation forest using cryptographic manifests, invariants, and staged reservations. An evaluation across 32 registered decisions and external adapters demonstrated that the protocol successfully enforces population-safe succession and rejects semantic mutants.
7313d5e64734621e:2746.one_liner: Authorization succession protocols can secure self-modifying AI agent populations by binding authority across replacements, forks, and rollbacks.
7313d5e64734621e:2746.bottom_line: Managing authorization across self-modifying AI agent populations requires strict lineage binding and staged reservations to prevent unauthorized privilege accumulation.

claims.text: An independent checker accepts all 64 original traces and rejects 28/28 semantic mutants; 12/12 profile invariants, 16/16 crash cuts, and 32/32 contender schedules pass.
claims.support_span: An independent checker accepts all 64 original traces and rejects 28/28 semantic mutants; 12/12 profile invariants, 16/16 crash cuts, and 32/32 contender schedules pass.

f096ef7fd0ed3668:2747.summary: Computer-use agents (CUAs) use persistent workspace memory files that mix user instructions and external claims at the same privilege level, enabling persistent memory attacks where benign external content injects malicious instructions into memory. To mitigate this, researchers proposed ZoneClaw, which establishes memory-zoning with hierarchical trust zones and asymmetric privilege roles. External claims persist in a low-trust zone and must cross an explicit authority boundary to guide actions. Across evaluations, ZoneClaw drastically reduced attack success rates while preserving agent utility.
f096ef7fd0ed3668:2747.one_liner: ZoneClaw mitigates persistent memory injection attacks in computer-use agents by separating low-trust workspace memory from high-trust execution authority.
f096ef7fd0ed3668:2747.bottom_line: Persistent memory attacks in computer-use agents can be effectively mitigated by enforcing strict memory-zoning and authority boundaries between ingested content and actionable execution.

claims.text: Across four attack scenarios, two injection settings, and four backbones, ZoneClaw drives ASR from 372/480 to 6/480 while retaining utility in 458/480 trials, and remains effective against some defense-aware attackers.
claims.support_span: Across four attack scenarios, two injection settings, and four backbones, ZoneClaw drives ASR from 372/480 to 6/480 while retaining utility in 458/480 trials, and remains effective against some defense-aware attackers.

key_facts: Attack Success Rate (ASR) reduction: from 372/480 down to 6/480

a5ec8ba43286576e:2715.summary: To address privacy risks and PII leakage in LLMs deployed in sensitive domains, researchers introduced Locket (LoRA-Oriented Control via Keyed Entry Tokens). Locket trains fine-grained LoRA adapters representing different access policies, paired with a gating module that associates a keyed entry token with a specific adapter via hard routing. A valid token unlocks private knowledge, while a missing or invalid token triggers a privacy-preserving adapter that redacts sensitive content. Evaluations across models like Qwen3, Llama-3.2, and Gemma-2 showed that Locket maintains utility when tokens are valid and substantially reduces PII leakage when tokens are absent.
a5ec8ba43286576e:2715.one_liner: Locket provides fine-grained, token-gated access control for LLMs using LoRA adapters to prevent PII leakage without sacrificing utility.
a5ec8ba43286576e:2715.bottom_line: Tokenized key-gated LoRA adapter routing allows enterprises to enforce strict access control over private data inside LLMs without retraining base models.

claims.text: Our extensive experiments demonstrate that, when the correct token is provided, Locket preserves perplexity comparable to fine-tuning on raw data (without any defense).
claims.support_span: Our extensive experiments demonstrate that, when the correct token is provided, Locket preserves perplexity comparable to fine-tuning on raw data (without any defense).

key_facts: Evaluated models: Qwen3 (1.7B and 8B), Llama-3.2 (1B and 3B), Gemma-2-2B

3760b79ae828ac9b:2540.summary: Tool-using agents can output citations and execution logs that remain structurally valid while being mismatched or transplanted across claims, actions, or source versions. To address this, researchers introduced a claim-anchored execution contract that jointly binds emitted claims, exact source spans, ordered execution prefixes, and source access states into cryptographic receipts. A deterministic verifier reconstructs these bindings before semantic evaluation. Across 1,280 cross-object attacks, the joint contract detected 99.61% of substitutions.
3760b79ae828ac9b:2540.one_liner: Claim-anchored execution contracts prevent citation and evidence tampering in tool-using agents by cryptographically binding claims to their execution traces and source spans.
3760b79ae828ac9b:2540.bottom_line: Auditing tool-using agents requires jointly binding claims, source evidence, and execution traces to prevent citation-transplantation attacks.

claims.text: Across 1,280 cross-object attacks, the joint contract detects 1,275 substitutions (0.9961).
claims.support_span: Across 1,280 cross-object attacks, the joint contract detects 1,275 substitutions (0.9961).

b044d2469ff235f4:2638.summary: Researchers introduced Praxa, an agent harness designed to make the states of an LLM agent—ranging from action proposals and authority checks to external read-backs and reviewed promotions—explicit through deterministic admission and brokered execution. Evaluation results across internal unit tests, Terminal-Bench pilots, and coordination-proxy comparisons demonstrated that while Praxa establishes an evidence-bound architecture for authority-to-effect transitions, current data does not establish improved quality, adversarial security, or production safety lift.
b044d2469ff235f4:2638.one_liner: Praxa provides an evidence-bound harness architecture for governed AI agent execution, making authority-to-effect transitions explicit and testable.
b044d2469ff235f4:2638.bottom_line: Governing AI agent execution requires architectural separation between action proposals, authority checks, and verified external effects.

claims.text: First, an author-run repository-local audit at a pinned revision passed 1,027/1,027 unit tests and 89/89 Workerd tests, instrumented all 363 expected source files, and met four coverage floors; raw per-test transcripts and independent reproduction are unavailable.
claims.support_span: First, an author-run repository-local audit at a pinned revision passed 1,027/1,027 unit tests and 89/89 Workerd tests, instrumented all 363 expected source files, and met four coverage floors; raw per-test transcripts and independent reproduction are unavailable.

67ac19568dcc6aa1:2730.summary: Agent developers frequently evaluate prompts, tools, and debuggers using simulator-grounded verifiers. However, if verifier probes or predicates encode target identities, an optimizer can appear effective without resolving genuine ambiguity—essentially because the verifier leaked the answer. The authors discovered this failure mode in a closed-loop agent debugger and replaced solver-first evaluation with a support-gated verification contract that verifies evidence eligibility and non-revelation before component optimization.
67ac19568dcc6aa1:2730.one_liner: Verifiers in agent debugging can accidentally leak answers and invalidate solver evaluations unless evidence eligibility is strictly gated.
67ac19568dcc6aa1:2730.bottom_line: Agent optimization benchmarks are flawed if the underlying verifier leaks target identities, necessitating support-gated verification contracts before running solvers.

claims.text: A subsequent audit found that exact-anchor predicates produced the planted pair in 9/9 cases.
claims.support_span: A subsequent audit found that exact-anchor predicates produced the planted pair in 9/9 cases.

1df3ee805a6bd359:1740.summary: Researchers introduced EviGraph for proof-carrying selective recommendation over temporal public-service knowledge graphs. Public-service recommendations require strict evidence matching service scope and dates, but treating every missing detail as decisive can cause unnecessary abstention. EviGraph distinguishes critical decision requirements from non-essential information using a language agent linked to a temporal knowledge graph, with a deterministic checker verifying support. Evaluation on a Hong Kong public-service benchmark showed that this approach reduces unnecessary abstention.
1df3ee805a6bd359:1740.one_liner: EviGraph uses a language agent and temporal knowledge graphs to reduce unnecessary abstention in evidence-based public-service recommendations.
1df3ee805a6bd359:1740.bottom_line: Reliable evidence-based recommendations require explicitly defining critical decision requirements rather than applying rigid verification to every missing detail.

claims.text: Evaluation on a bilingual Hong Kong public-service benchmark with executable policy references shows that this distinction reduces unnecessary abstention.
claims.support_span: Evaluation on a bilingual Hong Kong public-service benchmark with executable policy references shows that this distinction reduces unnecessary abstention.

80892eda7e1f5aab:2586.summary: Researchers formulated grounded correction arbitration for text-based embodied agents to determine how an agent should respond when a user's correction might be incorrect. They implemented GAVA, which uses observation-bounded evidence, legal probes, and a one-step expected-loss rule to choose among accepting, rejecting, inspecting the world, or asking the speaker. Evaluations in text-based ALFWorld showed high correction accuracy, though results did not establish a general advantage of environmental value of information over clarification.
80892eda7e1f5aab:2586.one_liner: GAVA provides a principled arbitration framework for text-based embodied agents to evaluate potentially incorrect user corrections using observation bounds.
80892eda7e1f5aab:2586.bottom_line: Embodied agents can reliably arbitrate conflicting user corrections by combining observation-bounded evidence with expected-loss decision rules.

claims.text: Semantic GAVA makes four factual errors in each cohort, corresponding to 98.8 percent and 98.7 percent accuracy, and all methods complete every task.

f7cf8f6241f5d2db:2035.summary: Multi-agent systems often face a safety dilemma where benign individual contributions jointly enable prohibited actions, but blocking all sensitive actions hinders collaboration. To solve this, researchers introduce authorization-paired evaluation along with the FlowReview framework, combining object resolution, permission ranking, and deterministic enforcement. In controlled composition experiments, reviewing combined artifacts successfully reduced the denied-commit rate from 86.0% down to zero without causing any loss in authorized supply. These findings demonstrate that preserving object identity and permission linkage through verifiable components is crucial for secure multi-agent governance.
f7cf8f6241f5d2db:2035.one_liner: FlowReview introduces an authorization-paired framework that eliminates false-positive blocked commits in multi-agent workflows.
f7cf8f6241f5d2db:2035.bottom_line: Multi-agent systems can safely collaborate without excessive blocking if authorization and object identity are strictly paired with verifiable execution components.

68db07d2bbf4fcc7:1910.summary: Large Language Models can be implanted with backdoors during training that trigger unwanted behavior, while existing defenses often inadvertently degrade model performance on benign prompts. To resolve this, researchers propose NEEDLE, a training-free method for targeted backdoor removal using activation vectors to estimate backdoor directions and refusal subspaces. By applying sequential weight orthogonalisation, NEEDLE suppresses the backdoor without requiring a clean reference model or original poisoned data. Evaluations across multiple model families show that NEEDLE achieves a 0% attack success rate on challenging code injection attacks while maintaining minimal KL divergence and preserving model capabilities.
68db07d2bbf4fcc7:1910.one_liner: NEEDLE removes LLM backdoors via weight orthogonalisation without requiring reference models or hurting benign performance.
68db07d2bbf4fcc7:1910.bottom_line: Targeted LLM backdoors can be completely neutralized via weight orthogonalisation without sacrificing general model capabilities or requiring clean reference data.

c828fdddd42f8ffa:2182.summary: Reasoning over incomplete chemical representations like Markush structures remains a challenge for AI-driven scientific discovery, as variable R-group placeholders require grounding across multiple modalities. To address the lack of specialized evaluation, researchers introduce R-GroundBench, a diagnostic benchmark featuring a Multiple-Choice VQA track and an open-ended generation track built from real patent data. Experimental results reveal a large performance drop when moving from easy tasks to hard VQA tasks, and generation exact match remains below 20% for most models. These findings show that current AI systems still lack reliable grounding and execution capabilities for complex molecular editing.
c828fdddd42f8ffa:2182.one_liner: R-GroundBench exposes severe grounding and reasoning limitations in AI models attempting complex Markush molecular editing.
c828fdddd42f8ffa:2182.bottom_line: Current vision-language and language models lack reliable R-group grounding for chemical representations, exposing major reliability gaps in AI-driven drug discovery.

d72c3221552b0c56:2526.summary: Quantized large language models deployed on edge devices are highly vulnerable to jailbreak attacks because quantization weakens their alignment safeguards. To fix this without heavy computational overhead, researchers introduce MOMAT, a hardware-enhanced safety framework combining structured knowledge retrieval with low-power Compute-in-Memory acceleration. MOMAT maps semantic clusters into multiple atlases and uses a lightweight Mixture of Experts detector to guard prompts efficiently. Evaluations show that MOMAT accelerates retrieval by millions of times and drastically cuts energy consumption while matching state-of-the-art defense performance.
d72c3221552b0c56:2526.one_liner: MOMAT secures edge-deployed quantized LLMs against jailbreaks with massive speedups using Compute-in-Memory acceleration.
d72c3221552b0c56:2526.bottom_line: Hardware-accelerated Compute-in-Memory retrieval can make edge-deployed quantized LLMs both robust against jailbreaks and highly energy-efficient.

1f94155a570b5733:2520.summary: The proliferation of AI-generated academic papers has introduced scientific slop, where individual sections look plausible but the global scientific reasoning breaks down. Conventional token-based detectors fail to catch these flaws, but researchers have constructed SciSlopBench using 390 AI-generated papers to benchmark structural and argumentative failures. Their measures identify AI papers with 85.9% accuracy, significantly outperforming existing baselines like Binoculars. To mitigate this issue without causing reward hacking, they propose SciSlopHarness, a framework that forces LLMs to revise text strictly grounded in experiment records.
1f94155a570b5733:2520.one_liner: SciSlopBench and SciSlopHarness benchmark and mitigate flawed scientific reasoning in AI-generated academic papers.
1f94155a570b5733:2520.bottom_line: Detecting and fixing AI-generated scientific slop requires global reasoning checks and strict evidentiary grounding rather than simple prose adjustments.

22c0e4941496884e:2742.summary: As code generation is increasingly delegated to AI systems, oversight bottlenecks reveal a fundamental vocabulary gap between cybernetic actions and epistemic understanding. Current oversight often accepts approval-shaped outputs that satisfy rubber-stamping requirements without verifying the underlying reasoning. To address this, the authors propose a governance criterion requiring consequential choices to carry verifiable conditions and introduce a reconstruction test alongside an ORRCF deliberation-recording convention. These tools ensure third parties can independently audit agentic decisions instead of blindly approving them.
22c0e4941496884e:2742.one_liner: A new vocabulary and auditing framework helps developers verify AI agent decisions rather than relying on rubber-stamping.
22c0e4941496884e:2742.bottom_line: Effective oversight of agentic AI code generation requires recording retrievable reasoning paths instead of relying on superficial approval checkboxes.

142355993db75860:2733.summary: Agentic AI deployments combine language model inference with tool execution, retrieval, and external access, creating complex security-relevant deviations across entire workflows. To monitor these processes, researchers propose the Agentic-Process Intrusion Detection System (A-IDS), an evidence-aware security layer that compares observed runtime behavior against versioned expectation baselines. A-IDS tracks workflow states, authorization, and communications while explicitly separating evidence capture from operational impact. The model treats prompt injection not just as an input anomaly, but as a potential origin for cascading cross-agent process deviations.
142355993db75860:2733.one_liner: A-IDS introduces runtime monitoring and evidence-based intrusion detection for multi-step agentic workflows.
142355993db75860:2733.bottom_line: Securing multi-step agentic workflows requires runtime monitoring engines that evaluate evidence-supported process trajectories rather than isolated inputs.

4b9162604f2e157c:2143.summary: Cyber attack agents are traditionally trained and evaluated inside isolated simulators, making it difficult to transfer learned policies across environments with different state representations and action spaces. Researchers demonstrate that simulator-to-simulator and simulator-to-real policy transfers can be treated as an alignment problem by separating state alignment from action translation. Evaluating across four cyber platforms including CyberBattleSim and NASim, zero-shot transfer successfully preserved performance and achieved strong behavioral similarity in emulated virtual machines. These findings prove that RL cyber agents can be ported to new environments without full retraining.
4b9162604f2e157c:2143.one_liner: A new framework enables zero-shot policy transfer for reinforcement learning cyber attack agents across different simulation platforms.
4b9162604f2e157c:2143.bottom_line: Cyber attack reinforcement learning agents can successfully transfer learned policies across different simulation platforms without retraining by decoupling state alignment from action translation.

2eb4f0233c4a822c:2549.summary: Fine-tuning Large Language Models can inadvertently recover private information that was supposedly scrubbed or inaccessible through direct model queries. Previous extraction attacks required genuine private training supervision, but researchers now demonstrate that data-free model generation can supply sufficient supervision via task structuring and answer likelihood filtering. Proposing a data-free attack called ReGap, the authors show that fine-tuning with low-rank adaptation significantly improves target association recovery across multiple open model families. This privacy risk proves that standard model customization routines can reawaken latent sensitive data memorized during initial pre-training.
2eb4f0233c4a822c:2549.one_liner: ReGap demonstrates that data-free fine-tuning can extract private training data from language models without original supervision sets.
2eb4f0233c4a822c:2549.bottom_line: Routine model fine-tuning and customization can easily reawaken latent privacy risks and extract forgotten data from language models.

c7c10a69afb84267:2535.summary: As AI agents delegate tasks across concurrent and failure-prone distributed workers, resource limits act as vital authorization boundaries to prevent catastrophic overspending. However, dropped messages, network partitions, and delayed timeouts can still corrupt credit ledgers and break budget conservation. Researchers formalize fault-tolerant budget conservation for multi-agent delegation by using exclusive escrow credits, signed dispatch permits, and operation reservations bound to lineage keys. Formal proofs and crash-injected SQLite experiments demonstrate that this mechanism reliably prevents budget amplification and handles failures safely.

c7c10a69afb84267:2535.bottom_line: Distributed multi-agent systems must enforce cryptographic escrow credits and signed dispatch permits to prevent severe resource overspending during network partitions and crashes.

0e425e4cc95c4a48:2448.summary: When curating mathematical training data for Large Language Models, developers typically organize examples by topic, but reasoning approach offers an alternative matching principle. Researchers evaluated counterbalanced experimental designs comparing same-approach sources against same-topic sources across multiple mathematical domains and base models. The results show that fine-tuning models on data sharing the same solution method consistently outperforms topic-matched data across all evaluations. These findings prove that matching reasoning approaches yields superior mathematical knowledge transfer than matching topics alone.

0e425e4cc95c4a48:2448.bottom_line: Curating mathematical training data by solution method rather than topic yields significantly better knowledge transfer during LLM fine-tuning.

06f298801192d53c:2316.summary: Safety-aligned Large Language Models remain vulnerable to fine-tuning attacks, yet practical training pipelines typically rely on quality-based data filtering to remove harmful examples. Researchers evaluate these filtering pipelines and discover that while overt samples are removed, certain retained high-quality samples still degrade model safety due to layer-wise gradient patterns. To exploit this loophole, the authors propose Bi-Stage Quality-Constrained Safety-Degradation Text Optimization (Bi-QSTO), which optimizes poisoned samples to survive strict quality filters. Experiments show that even with 90% filtering rates, Bi-QSTO successfully retains high effectiveness across target models.

d16dd05f15010981:1788.summary: Traditional Machine Learning Network Intrusion Detection Systems require extensive labeled datasets, whereas Large Language Model detectors incur high costs and latency. To bridge this gap, researchers introduce JEV-IDS, an open experimental network intrusion detection system powered by the Jev System One Model for zero-day threat detection under label scarcity. JEV-IDS evaluates serialized network flow records to output binary attack probabilities and traffic categories. Evaluations on an NSL-KDD benchmark split show that JEV-IDS is significantly faster and cheaper than large cloud models while drastically reducing false alarms compared to random forest classifiers.

469443f9e5466e36:2373.summary: Decentralized agent economies frequently stitch together independent protocols to complete multi-step tasks, creating a risk where each step looks valid yet the overall outcome fails. For example, escrow contracts may release funds upon an authorized approval that lacks actual evidence of task completion. To analyze this, researchers systematize security and economic requirements across the agent task lifecycle into 17 property families and introduce guarantee closure as a task-relative evaluation criterion. Analyzing 12 systems and 840 matched executions, the study exposes frequent communication failures between verification and settlement stages. These findings highlight the architectural repairs needed to preserve end-to-end cryptographic and economic guarantees.

469443f9e5466e36:2373.bottom_line: Decentralized agent systems suffer from critical disconnects between verification and settlement that require rigorous guarantee closure enforcement.

84ff584988a33e1a:1261.summary: Ubuntu has issued a security notice detailing vulnerabilities discovered in OpenSSL concerning its QUIC stream implementation.
